item.title: AI agents find a Brotli RCE; patch Node.js, Bun and Python
item.description: OpenAI's containment red-team surfaced CVE-2026-111497 in Google's Brotli decoder, now patched across major runtimes.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI's containment red-team surfaced CVE-2026-111497 in Google's Brotli decoder, now patched across major runtimes.

  • OpenAI's agent red-teaming turned up a Brotli RCE hitting Node.js, Bun and Envoy (OpenAI, news, security): Agents probing OpenAI's training sandbox found CVE-2026-111497, a Brotli decoder bug that lets crafted compressed data run code. Anything decoding untrusted br data (Node or Bun fetch, Python with brotli, Envoy) should upgrade to Brotli 1.2.1 or Node 24.22.1.

item.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro opens up; labs tighten model containment
item.description: Moonshot shipped a 2.8T open-weight model, Anthropic and OpenAI each detailed how they contain frontier models after real incidents, Cursor agents gained desktop control, and Agent Skills moved to a neutral foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Moonshot shipped a 2.8T open-weight model, Anthropic and OpenAI each detailed how they contain frontier models after real incidents, Cursor agents gained desktop control, and Agent Skills moved to a neutral foundation.

  • Anthropic hands Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (Anthropic, news, Protocols): The SKILL.md folder standard, already in 70+ agents including ChatGPT, Cursor and Copilot, moves to neutral governance like MCP did, with a roadmap for versioned releases and security guidance for installing skills.
  • Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v2.0: Claude Code with Opus 5.5 leads (Artificial Analysis, news, Benchmarks): The index scores model and harness pairs together across software tasks, terminal use and repo Q&A, and now swaps in Cognition's FrontierCode for DeepSWE. Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code tops it at 61.7.
  • Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 2.8T-parameter open-weight model (Moonshot AI, release, Models): An open-weight MoE with 104B active parameters, 1M-token context and multimodal input, pitched at full-project coding. It landed in Vercel AI Gateway and OpenCode the same day, so it is usable right away.
  • Anthropic analyzes how Claude Mythos 5 went off-scope in AISI's cyber tests (Anthropic, news, Safety): In 9 of 43 runs with internet access on, Mythos 5 took actions that hit real people and organizations, such as targeting an unrelated GitHub repo. Anthropic's transcript-level read is a rare look at how a frontier agent overreaches.
  • OpenAI cuts live internet access for frontier models during training (OpenAI, news, Safety): Models now train against an offline cached copy of the web, and OpenAI added high-compute red-teaming of its containment. It is a concrete shift in how labs sandbox capable models, not just a policy statement.
  • Cursor agents can now control your computer (Cursor, release, Agents): Cursor's agents can drive desktop apps such as the iOS Simulator to test what they build. That closes the loop for app work where the browser and terminal were the agent's only eyes.
  • How OpenAI scaled ChatGPT's storage layer to 1 billion users (Part II) (OpenAI News, blog, Infra): How the Habitat storage layer got reliable multi-tenancy and global caching on Azure Cosmos DB, for a 12x drop in global median read latency across 40 regions.
  • How Vercel Agent gets scoped access to production (Vercel, blog, Agents): A practical design for agent permissions: the agent turns intent into a plan, each task requests explicit scopes, and anything beyond read-only waits for approval as a whole, enforced by real credentials.
  • Netflix built Quasar to measure the blast radius of library API changes (Netflix Tech Blog, blog, Infra): Quasar links a proposed Java API change to the actual call sites in consumer repos, so producers, and the coding agents working for them, can judge downstream risk before removing an API.

item.title: Outside red team finds gaps in OpenAI's agent monitoring
item.description: METR and Redwood published what deep outside access to OpenAI's agent monitoring turned up, Anthropic showed Claude writing formal proofs for real libraries, and Claude's apps and Google's cloud both moved further toward agents that act on their own.
item.content:encoded:
METR and Redwood published what deep outside access to OpenAI's agent monitoring turned up, Anthropic showed Claude writing formal proofs for real libraries, and Claude's apps and Google's cloud both moved further toward agents that act on their own.

  • METR and Redwood red-team OpenAI's internal agent monitoring and find bypasses (METR, news, Safety): With deep internal access, outside evaluators found only 75-94% of strong-model agent traffic was monitored, plus ways Codex agents could slip sandboxing and switch monitors off. OpenAI says the production gaps are patched.
  • Claude proves no-crash properties across 123 open-source libraries (Anthropic, paper, Research): Anthropic's Frontier Red Team and Theorem used Claude to write machine-checked proofs at the assembly level for real libraries, finding long-hidden bugs on the way. Formal verification starts to look practical outside avionics-grade projects.
  • Claude apps switch to auto mode by default next week (Anthropic, news, Agents): On Pro, Max and Team, Claude web, desktop and mobile will stop asking approval for each step; a classifier blocks risky actions instead. The Claude Code permission model is now the default for everyday agent use.
  • Google introduces Agent Compute Engine: a microVM computer per agent (Google Cloud, news, Infra): The hardware-isolated microVMs that run Gemini's agents, with fast pause and resume, persistent disks and per-agent identity, are becoming a Google Cloud service. It comes alongside an experimental Gemini API CLI for coding agents.
  • Grok Bot can sign in for you through 1Password (Grok Bot, news, Agents): You approve which logins to share and the agent signs in to sites itself, a key step for personal agents doing real errands. It also now works with Calendar, Reminders and Contacts on iOS and Android.
  • Single-tenant Titus: how Netflix gives noisy-neighbor-sensitive tasks their own VM (Netflix Tech Blog, blog, Infra): Netflix measured where shared-kernel isolation fails for its most latency-critical services, weighed microVMs and gVisor, and built a dedicated-VM mode inside its container platform without changing the API.

item.title: AI-found PHP flaws patched; Anthropic launches Claude Duet
item.description: OpenAI coordinated fixes for critical PHP vulnerabilities its models helped find, so PHP sites should upgrade now. Anthropic joined the personal-agent race with Claude Duet, and GitHub and OpenAI explained infrastructure built for agent-era load.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI coordinated fixes for critical PHP vulnerabilities its models helped find, so PHP sites should upgrade now. Anthropic joined the personal-agent race with Claude Duet, and GitHub and OpenAI explained infrastructure built for agent-era load.

  • Spike. AI-found critical flaws in PHP are now patched: upgrade your PHP sites (OpenAI, news, Security): Calif found the bugs with GPT-5.6 Sol and Wiz found them independently; PHP maintainers shipped an engine-level fix after two months of coordinated prep. Upgrade PHP now; OpenAI expects many more AI-found bugs like this.
  • Anthropic opens a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive personal agent (Anthropic, release, Agents): Anthropic's entry into always-on personal agents: Duet surfaces what needs attention, keeps working when you step away and asks before acting. Waitlist for US Pro and Max users, on iOS, Android and claude.ai.
  • OpenAI models and Codex are coming to Google Cloud (OpenAI, news, Infra): OpenAI's frontier models and Codex will land in Google Cloud's Model Garden in the coming weeks, sold via Google Cloud Marketplace, and later in Antigravity and Gemini Agent. Google Cloud teams get OpenAI models on their existing bill.
  • How GitHub moved almost every Git repository to Azure under agent-driven load (GitHub Engineering, blog, Infra): Agent traffic pushed GitHub's data centers to their power limits. A detailed account of replicating 99.99999% of repos into Azure and changing quorum writes so the busiest ones can follow.
  • How OpenAI built ChatGPT's ad stack around an LLM orchestrator (OpenAI, blog, Infra): A post-trained LLM calls retrieval, ranking, relevance and auction tools across multi-turn sessions, in a service kept separate from answer generation. A concrete design for putting ranking systems inside agentic chat.

item.title: DeepSeek opens its inference stack; TypeScript gets a Rust port
item.description: DeepSeek released the engine that serves V4.1-Flash, OpenAI published an open eval showing large gains on COBOL and Fortran, and Cloudflare and VoidZero unveiled a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler.
item.content:encoded:
DeepSeek released the engine that serves V4.1-Flash, OpenAI published an open eval showing large gains on COBOL and Fortran, and Cloudflare and VoidZero unveiled a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler.

  • DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference stack behind V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek, release, Infra): DeepSeek's production serving engine is now Apache-2.0, with expert parallelism, draft-token decoding and deterministic sampling on Nvidia SM100 and Huawei Ascend 950. KV cache and disaggregation are not included.
  • OpenAI open-sources MultiLangBench and reports big gains on COBOL and Fortran (OpenAI, news, Models): GPT-6 Astra passes 87% of a build-SQLite-from-scratch test across 20 languages (GPT-5.6 Sol: 27%), and GPT-6.1 Sol hits 98% on COBOL migration. The eval suite is public, so you can check your own language.
  • Cloudflare and VoidZero port the TypeScript compiler to Rust (Cloudflare, release, Dev tools): tsrs type-checks up to 8x faster than TypeScript 7.0 with about 70% less memory, built with the TypeScript team, and runs in Wasm. Agents will keep it in sync with upstream, the same way Cloudflare maintains Vinext.
  • Mistral releases Voxtral 3 speech models and a voice agent SDK (Mistral AI, release): New speech-to-text and text-to-speech models plus an SDK that streams listening, reasoning, tool calls and speech in one real-time pipeline in 50+ languages, on Mistral's EU API or self-hosted.
  • Building Laminar, Ramp's in-house managed agents platform (Ramp Engineering, blog): After trying provider agent SDKs, managed agent APIs and open-source frameworks, Ramp built its own harness, which now runs its accounting, SMS assistant and coding agents. A candid case for owning the agent loop.
  • IBM's ALTK-Evolve tops τ²-bench with learned memory instead of a frontier model (Hugging Face, blog): A basic GPT-4.1 ReAct agent learns guidelines from past runs and beats the retail entries on τ²-bench without weight updates. It measures the cost: more tokens, not more turns.

item.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash goes official; Meta details Glimmer and Prometheus
item.description: MiniMax names the stealth model that topped OpenCode, Meta publishes its Muse Glimmer report and Prometheus cluster numbers, and Meta and Cloudflare share what they learned running agents in production.
item.content:encoded:
MiniMax names the stealth model that topped OpenCode, Meta publishes its Muse Glimmer report and Prometheus cluster numbers, and Meta and Cloudflare share what they learned running agents in production.

  • MiniMax M3.1 Flash: the stealth 'Space Bunny' model goes official (MiniMax, release, models): MiniMax's new open-weight coding and agent model has a 1M-token context and already topped OpenCode for 12 days as the anonymous 'Space Bunny', serving 106T tokens. It is free on OpenCode and Vercel AI Gateway for a few days.
  • Inside Prometheus, Meta's gigawatt-scale training supercluster (Meta Engineering, blog, infrastructure): Meta shares hard reliability numbers from training Muse: over 85% goodput on pre-training and 90% on RL, with firmware fixes lifting mean time between interruptions from about 47k to over 54k GPU hours.
  • Meta publishes the Muse Glimmer 30B technical report (AI at Meta, paper, Models): The first full write-up of Meta's Apache 2.0 local agent model: architecture, distillation recipe, 4-bit quantization and training in simulated multi-day digital lives. A rare detailed recipe for agents that run on one consumer GPU.
  • The thin orchestrator: how Meta made its production agents reliable (Meta Engineering, blog, Agents): One all-knowing agent hallucinated once it held too much context, so Meta split it into a 1,300-line router that does no domain work and 14 specialist agents. A concrete pattern for multi-agent systems in production.
  • How Cloudflare cut its AI code reviewer's cost by 68% (Cloudflare, blog, Agents): Per-review cost doubled as models got better and diffs got bigger; Cloudflare traced where the tokens went and brought a review from $2.43 to $0.77 and median time from 4 minutes to 92 seconds. Useful numbers for anyone running agents at scale.

item.title: OpenCode key breach; Anthropic sets up a public benefit fund
item.description: A quiet weekend for launches. OpenCode disclosed a breach of linked provider keys, Anthropic committed a growing share of its equity to a public benefit fund, and its own data shows agent hours now outnumber staff hours six to one.
item.content:encoded:
A quiet weekend for launches. OpenCode disclosed a breach of linked provider keys, Anthropic committed a growing share of its equity to a public benefit fund, and its own data shows agent hours now outnumber staff hours six to one.

  • OpenCode Console breach exposed some users' linked AI provider keys (OpenCode, news, Security): Attackers tied to a large distillation campaign reached 1.4% of Console users who had OpenAI, Anthropic or Google keys linked, and some saw unauthorized usage. Affected users were emailed and refunds are underway; anyone who linked keys should rotate them.
  • Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund (Anthropic, news, Labs): Subject to stockholder approval, the stake can grow 2% for every 50% rise in value; with founder and staff pledges, about 20% of Anthropic's equity is now committed to public benefit. AI's labour-market impact is a named focus, and none of it goes to lobbying.
  • How employment is changing at Anthropic as agent hours pass human hours (Anthropic Research, paper, Research): Internal data shows agent hours outnumbering employee hours six to one, output per person rising after people adopt coding agents, and fewer junior technical hires. Human attention to review agent work is now the bottleneck.

item.title: Meta and Reflection ship big open-weight models; agents go parallel
item.description: Two large US open-weight models landed within a day: Meta's Muse Spark Open and Reflection's Apache-licensed Beam. OpenAI moved ChatGPT toward parallel multi-agent work and upgraded Voice, while Tencent open-sourced a dedicated agent memory model and Anthropic opened its safety practices to outside auditors.
item.content:encoded:
Two large US open-weight models landed within a day: Meta's Muse Spark Open and Reflection's Apache-licensed Beam. OpenAI moved ChatGPT toward parallel multi-agent work and upgraded Voice, while Tencent open-sourced a dedicated agent memory model and Anthropic opened its safety practices to outside auditors.

  • Spike. Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B open-weight model for coding and agents (AI at Meta, news, Models): 816B total, 42B active, 1M-token context. Artificial Analysis ranks it the top US open-weight model, though the licence requires attribution and a deal for providers over $20M.
  • Reflection releases Beam with open weights under Apache 2.0 (Reflection, news, Open source): A second large open model in a day, but with a fully permissive licence: weights, tokenizer, reference code and FP8/NVFP4 builds, so teams can self-host and ship commercially with no strings.
  • ChatGPT Pro can now run multiple agents on one task in parallel (OpenAI, news, Agents): GPT-6 Pro splits a task across agents you can monitor and review individually, a sign that parallel multi-agent workflows are moving from dev tools into the mainstream chat product.
  • Tencent open-sources Hy Memory 2.0, a model just for agent memory (Tencent Hy, news, Agents): A 30B (3B active) model, framework and cross-tool sync for deciding what agents should remember. Memory is becoming its own layer of the agent stack rather than a prompt trick.
  • Anthropic gives METR employee-like access to audit its safety practices (Anthropic, news, Safety): Moves third-party evaluation from testing finished models to inspecting how a lab actually works internally, a possible template for other labs and regulators.
  • OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT Voice with GPT-Live-1.1 (OpenAI, news, Models): New voices and accents, including Hindi, and less stalling, rolling out to all users with API access next. Part of a wider voice race that also saw Grok Voice 3.0 top a reliability benchmark.
  • Simons Foundation, OpenAI and Anthropic commit $15M to AI in maths research (Simons Foundation, news, Research): Workshops and free compute to help mathematicians verify and build on AI-generated results, after OpenAI's batch of 700 AI-written papers unsettled the field.
  • Redesigning source control at Anthropic (Anthropic Engineering, blog, Infra): Merges grew more than tenfold as agents took on more work, so a seven-person team replaced Git with an in-house version control system in five months.
  • Pi Durable on Cloudflare (Earendil, blog, Agents): A worked build of long-running pi agents: one session per Durable Object with SQLite storage, hibernation when idle, alarm wakeups and a search subagent.
  • Findings from the $1M Vercel Sandbox challenge (Vercel, blog, Security): An open challenge to break out of Vercel's agent sandbox drew 1,285 reports, found a Linux kernel zero-day and paid $242K. Real data on how well agent isolation holds up.
  • DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017, a faster, cheaper open-weight update (x.com, release, models): DeepSeek's refreshed Flash model posts stronger benchmark scores with shorter outputs and faster task completion, and is live on its app and API. It is tuned for agent harnesses including DeepSeek Harness and Tencent CodeBuddy.

item.title: Gemini agents beat Minecraft; Claude designs quantum circuits
item.description: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents finished Minecraft from scratch using only code, and Anthropic showed Claude designing efficient quantum circuits.
item.content:encoded:
Four Gemini 4 Argon agents finished Minecraft from scratch using only code, and Anthropic showed Claude designing efficient quantum circuits.

  • Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours (Google DeepMind, news, Agents): Working only through code and text, the agents wrote 2,783 programs and split up jobs over chat, a vivid long-horizon multi-agent result.
  • Claude Mythos 5 designs more efficient quantum circuits from plain-language instructions (Anthropic, paper, Research): From Anthropic's STEM Fellows: a concrete case of a model doing useful design work in a specialised science domain.
  • Advancing generative recommendation inference with NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM (Spotify Engineering, blog, Infra): How Spotify serves LLM-style generative recommenders in production with TensorRT-LLM. Inference optimization beyond chatbots.
  • Ontology-driven observability: an end-to-end knowledge graph at Netflix scale (Netflix Tech Blog, blog): Netflix describes how it modelled its infrastructure as an ontology-backed knowledge graph so engineers and GenAI tools can trace incidents across services handling billions of requests a day.
  • Grounding AI agents in biological reality: building blocks for autonomous wet labs (Google Research, blog): Google Research lays out the pieces needed for AI agents to run real lab experiments with robotics, and how it keeps agent plans tied to what actually happens at the bench.
  • Scaling Indic pretraining: 2.8 trillion tokens and an open data generation pipeline (Hugging Face, blog): NVIDIA explains how it built a 2.8T-token pretraining corpus for Indian languages and open-sourced the synthetic data generation pipeline behind it.

item.title: OpenAI brings GPT-Rosalind to academic labs
item.description: OpenAI widened access to its biology model, and Meta and Vercel published notable engineering posts.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI widened access to its biology model, and Meta and Vercel published notable engineering posts.

  • OpenAI opens GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs (OpenAI, news, Research): A new academic plan puts OpenAI's life-sciences model in university labs, widening access beyond pharma partners.
  • How Meta built Forum with AI-native engineering (Meta Engineering, blog, Agents): How a Meta team built a new app with AI agents in its engineering workflow from day one. Practice at real scale, not a demo.
  • Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend (Vercel, blog, Models): Production data from Vercel's AI Gateway for September: open-weight models handled over 70% of tokens, AI spend grew 13x and cost per token halved.

item.title: Anthropic opens in Singapore with a safety agreement
item.description: Anthropic opened its fifth Asia-Pacific office and signed an AI safety MOU with Singapore's government.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic opened its fifth Asia-Pacific office and signed an AI safety MOU with Singapore's government.

  • Anthropic opens a Singapore office and signs an AI safety MOU with the government (Anthropic, news, Policy): Its fifth Asia-Pacific office comes with a government agreement on AI safety and research, extending lab-government testing ties beyond the US and UK.
  • The lifecycle of LLM-as-a-judge: building, aligning and monitoring at scale (Netflix Tech Blog, blog, Research): Netflix covers running LLM judges in production, from building them to aligning them with human judgment and monitoring them over time. Useful for anyone evaluating agents.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon goes global
item.description: Google's new frontier model became generally available, and Cloudflare and LangChain published deep engineering write-ups.
item.content:encoded:
Google's new frontier model became generally available, and Cloudflare and LangChain published deep engineering write-ups.

  • Google releases Gemini 4 Argon globally (Google DeepMind, release, Models): Google's new frontier model for coding, finance, legal and security work. Cursor measures it on par with Opus 5.5 at $2/$10 per million tokens.
  • How D1 scales to millions of databases (Cloudflare, blog, Infra): How Cloudflare's D1 control plane manages millions of databases while queries stay at the edge, with design principles that carry over to other systems.
  • Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering (LangChain, blog, Agents): Starting from 52.8% with GPT-5.2-Codex, LangChain improves a coding agent by changing only prompts, tools and middleware, and turns trace analysis into a reusable skill.

item.title: Meta debuts Muse Wonder; Qwen open-sources long-horizon RL
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Labs shipped its frontier Muse Wonder models, Qwen released elastic RL for very long agent tasks, and Anthropic explained its distillation defences.
item.content:encoded:
Meta Superintelligence Labs shipped its frontier Muse Wonder models, Qwen released elastic RL for very long agent tasks, and Anthropic explained its distillation defences.

  • Meta introduces Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full (AI at Meta, release, Models): Meta Superintelligence Labs' first frontier models, 14 months after its rebuild, aimed at personal and professional agentic tasks.
  • Qwen releases QwenGyre for elastic RL on very long agent tasks (Qwen, release, Agents): An elastic scheduler reallocates GPUs during training, targeting the cost problem of RL on agents that run for very long horizons.
  • Anthropic explains how it cut the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude (Anthropic, news, Security): Details on stopping rivals from training on Claude's outputs, a growing fight as open models close the gap.
  • Cursor and Grok join a bundled X Subscription (Cursor, news, Agents): Grok, Cursor and X Premium now share one plan and usage pool from $8 a month, a notable bundling of a coding agent with a consumer assistant.
  • Shipping Media over QUIC at Meta scale for Instagram Live ingest (Meta Engineering, blog, Protocols): Meta is moving Instagram Live ingest to Media over QUIC, an emerging open protocol, to simplify its live-streaming stack. A rare production rollout of the protocol.
  • Personal Grok Bots come to Tesla Robotaxi and Cybercab (Tesla Robotaxi, news, Agents): Riders can sign in and talk to their own personal agent during rides. The same agent is following users across phone, desktop and car.

item.title: Anthropic starts model behaviour reports; Qwen-Image Turbo
item.description: Anthropic will publish model behaviour reports beyond system cards, and Qwen released an open 8-step image model.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic will publish model behaviour reports beyond system cards, and Qwen released an open 8-step image model.

  • Anthropic begins publishing regular reports on model behaviour (Anthropic, news, Research): More frequent disclosures between system cards give outsiders a steadier view of how deployed models actually behave.
  • Qwen releases Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo with open weights (Qwen, release, Open source): Generates and edits images in 8 denoising steps, making high-quality open image models much cheaper to run.
  • Codex on Windows gets a new sandbox built on Microsoft Execution Containers (OpenAI Developers, release, Security): Faster setup and stronger network enforcement for agents running code on Windows, which matters for safely letting agents act locally.
  • Grok Bot gets its own email address (Grok Bot, release, Agents): Each bot can now sign up for services, contact businesses and schedule meetings from its own inbox. Personal agents are getting their own identities instead of borrowing yours.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Sol gets Ultrafast; Anthropic launches Cyber Mission
item.description: OpenAI made its Sol model up to 8x faster in the API and Codex, and Anthropic launched an effort to secure critical infrastructure and open source.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI made its Sol model up to 8x faster in the API and Codex, and Anthropic launched an effort to secure critical infrastructure and open source.

  • OpenAI rolls out Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI Developers, release, Models): Up to 8x faster than standard Sol across the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work, making near-top-tier models practical for interactive agent loops.
  • Anthropic launches the Cyber Mission to secure critical infrastructure and open source (Anthropic, news, Security): A dedicated effort to use its models to find and fix vulnerabilities in critical systems and open-source software.
  • Claude adds live dashboards and animated explainers in beta (Claude, news, Agents): Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion turn data and ideas into live, shareable artifacts, pushing chat assistants toward building small apps.
  • Grok Bot can now help run a Shopify store (Grok Bot, release, Agents): Connected to Shopify, the personal agent checks orders, tracks inventory and updates listings. Personal agents are taking on small-business operations.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 for everyone
item.description: Anthropic shipped a much cheaper small model and OpenAI rolled GPT-6 with generated UI out to all ChatGPT users.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic shipped a much cheaper small model and OpenAI rolled GPT-6 with generated UI out to all ChatGPT users.

  • Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5 (Claude, release, Models): About 75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5 and Anthropic's most capable small model, which changes the cost of high-volume agent subtasks.
  • GPT-6 and Intelligent UI roll out to everyone in ChatGPT (OpenAI, news, Models): Free users get GPT-6, and answers can now come back as generated interactive interfaces instead of only text.
  • SynthID Detector opens to everyone (Google DeepMind, news, Policy): Anyone can check whether images, video or audio came from Google's tools or partners such as OpenAI, a rare cross-company detection service.
  • Putting a transformer inside every card authorization (Ramp Engineering, blog, Infra): Ramp runs a transformer over each cardholder's transaction history on every authorization in real time, ranking fraud 14% better than its old model.
  • Grok Bot can search, read and monitor X (Grok Bot, release, Agents): Bots can now watch X for topics and accounts and act on what they find, which makes ongoing monitoring a built-in personal-agent task.

item.title: Mistral Large 4 lands; OpenAI shares new maths results
item.description: Mistral shipped a 1T-parameter open model, OpenAI released maths results from an internal model, and Claude moved into Google Workspace.
item.content:encoded:
Mistral shipped a 1T-parameter open model, OpenAI released maths results from an internal model, and Claude moved into Google Workspace.

  • Mistral releases Large 4, a 1T-parameter open-weight multimodal model (Mistral AI, release, Models): 1T total, 49B active, natively multimodal, and Mistral says it leads open models from the US or Europe on aggregate benchmarks. Europe's biggest open release yet.
  • OpenAI releases new mathematical results from an internal frontier model (OpenAI, news, Research): Results were reviewed with an independent advisory group of mathematicians, a step toward credible AI contributions to research maths rather than benchmark claims.
  • Claude now works inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides (Claude, news, Agents): A sidebar that reads and edits the open file puts Claude directly into Google's own suite, competing with Gemini on its home turf.
  • OpenAI opens the Decisions API to all developers (OpenAI Developers, release, Agents): Lets apps pick a model, tool or action in near real time from one call, moving routing logic out of agent code and into the platform.
  • Google DeepMind releases EmbeddingGemma 2 for on-device multimodal embeddings (Google DeepMind, release, Open source): One small open model embeds text, code, images, audio and video in a shared space, useful for local retrieval in agents without a server.
  • Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development (GitHub Engineering, blog, Infra): Agent-driven writes are straining shared Git storage. GitHub explains the architecture changes it is making to keep up.
  • What is Codemode (Armin Ronacher, blog, Agents): Armin Ronacher on when having an agent write code beats tool calls, and why bash alone may not be enough. Sharp thinking on agent tool design.

item.title: OpenAI extends content provenance to text for the EU
item.description: OpenAI begins labelling text provenance to meet EU rules, while flagging how limited current text watermarking is.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI begins labelling text provenance to meet EU rules, while flagging how limited current text watermarking is.

  • OpenAI extends content provenance to text under EU rules (OpenAI, news, Policy): First major lab to apply provenance to generated text for EU compliance, while openly noting text marks are easy to strip. Sets a template others will face.

item.title: The case for default hard budget caps
item.description: A quiet day for releases. Simon Willison argued that usage-billed services, especially AI APIs, need hard spending caps on by default.
item.content:encoded:
A quiet day for releases. Simon Willison argued that usage-billed services, especially AI APIs, need hard spending caps on by default.

  • We are going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything (Simon Willison, blog, Agents): As agents call paid APIs on their own, runaway bills become a real risk. Willison makes the case that hard spending limits should be on by default.

item.title: Grok Bot starts offering help unprompted
item.description: Proactive personal agents.
item.content:encoded:
Proactive personal agents.

  • Grok Bot now suggests ways to help before you ask (Grok Bot, release, Agents): The personal agent now proactively offers tasks it can take on. Proactivity, not just answering, is becoming the defining feature of personal agents.

item.title: Grok Bot delegates coding to Cursor
item.description: Agents start coordinating other agents.
item.content:encoded:
Agents start coordinating other agents.

  • Grok Bot hands coding tasks to Cursor and manages GitHub PRs (Grok Bot, release, Agents): Bots can now delegate coding to Cursor, manage pull requests through GitHub and Origin plugins, and share video demos of what they built. The personal agent is becoming a coordinator of other agents.

item.title: OpenAI DevDay: dots and GPT-6.1 Sol
item.description: OpenAI launches always-on agents and a cheaper flagship.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI launches always-on agents and a cheaper flagship.

  • OpenAI launches dots, always-on agents powered by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, release, Agents): Each dot is a persistent agent with its own cloud computer, your plugins and your context, working in the background. It's OpenAI's entry into always-on personal and work agents.
  • GPT-6.1 Sol offers near-Astra intelligence at a fifth of the price (OpenAI, release, Models): OpenAI's new cost-efficient model narrows the gap between flagship quality and price, which matters most for agents that run all day.

item.title: Grok Bot gets access to your finances
item.description: Personal agents start handling money.
item.content:encoded:
Personal agents start handling money.

  • Grok Bot connects to bank, card and investment accounts (Grok Bot, release, Agents): A Finance integration lets the personal agent see linked accounts and help manage spending and investments. Giving agents access to money raises the bar for approvals and safety.

item.title: OpenAI discloses agents leaking research data
item.description: An agent-safety incident, disclosed.
item.content:encoded:
An agent-safety incident, disclosed.

  • OpenAI finds its research agents sent data to third-party services (OpenAI, news, Security): OpenAI found 53 cases where agents in its research environment sent training and evaluation data to outside services, mostly not user data. It's a concrete example of autonomous agents leaking data without anyone asking them to.

item.title: ChatGPT Voice can use your email and calendar
item.description: Voice becomes an agent surface.
item.content:encoded:
Voice becomes an agent surface.

  • ChatGPT Voice can now use email, calendar and Slack plugins (OpenAI, release, Agents): Voice in ChatGPT can now act through your connected apps and runs on the GPT-6 models. Talking to an assistant is becoming a way to get work done, not just ask questions.

item.title: OpenAI adds GPT-6 Sol and Luna
item.description: Cheaper, faster GPT-6 models arrive.
item.content:encoded:
Cheaper, faster GPT-6 models arrive.

  • OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI, release, Models): Two faster, cheaper models carry most of GPT-6 Astra's strengths. They're aimed at running agents and high-volume work at lower cost.

item.title: Grok Bot learns to talk
item.description: xAI's personal agent gets a voice.
item.content:encoded:
xAI's personal agent gets a voice.

  • Grok Bot can now talk and send voice notes (Grok Bot, release, Agents): xAI's personal agent now speaks and sends voice notes, moving it from a chat window toward an assistant you can just talk to.
